NDIA-ICT-IDM-001
1. Governance, risk and exceptions
Governance, accountability, risk and exceptions

NDIA must govern identity and access management as a core internal control with named accountable owners, risk stewards and approved delegations. Identity risks, shared risks, residual risks and control exceptions must be assessed against NDIA's risk appetite, documented, time bound, treated or escalated before approval.
Applies to all identity services, access decisions, exceptions and shared identity risks.

NDIA-ICT-IDM-002
2. Third-party, supplier and procurement governance
Third-party, procurement, supplier and cloud identity governance

Procurements, contracts, cloud services and third-party arrangements involving NDIA identities, identity data, credentials or system access must include identity, privacy, security, audit, offboarding, breach-notification and subcontractor controls. Suppliers must comply with NDIA requirements, provide assurance evidence and support timely revocation, data return and risk reassessment through the contract lifecycle.
Applies to suppliers, contractors, partners, providers, outsourced identity services, subcontractors and cloud-hosted identity services.

NDIA-ICT-IDM-003
3. Classified, caveated and protected information access
Information classification, protected Agency information and lawful access

Access to NDIA information must be authorised according to information value, sensitivity, classification, caveat, metadata, lawful NDIS purpose, verified need-to-know, clearance or citizenship conditions and approved disclosure authority. Protected Agency information must only be accessed, used, disclosed or externally shared by authorised identities for approved roles, functions and recipients.
Applies to official, classified, caveated and protected Agency information, including participant data and external sharing.

NDIA-ICT-IDM-004
4. Identity proofing, assurance and authority verification
Identity proofing, verification, assurance, eligibility and authority

NDIA must use risk-based identity assurance before issuing or relying on an identity, credential or access right. Workforce, contractors, providers, representatives, participants, nominees, organisations and external verification services must be identity-proofed, eligibility or authority checked, fraud screened, and linked to verified evidence or authoritative sources using only necessary data and approved verification channels.
Applies to onboarding, Digital ID proofing levels, external verification checks, workforce access, provider access, participant and nominee identity, authority changes and high-risk recovery.

5. Clearance-dependent, temporary and remote access
Clearance, temporary, exceptional and remote access conditions

Access that depends on a security clearance, caveat condition, citizenship eligibility, temporary approval, waiver, remote location or facility arrangement must be blocked unless the required vetting, risk assessment, approvals, agreements, supervision, monitoring, expiry and withdrawal conditions are recorded and enforced in identity and access controls.
Applies to classified resources, clearance-required roles, temporary or provisional access, eligibility waivers, hosted work locations and international or remote access.

NDIA-ICT-IDM-006
6. Access lifecycle and least privilege
Access lifecycle, least privilege, role design and segregation of duties

All human and non-human access must be requested, approved, provisioned, changed, certified and removed through managed lifecycle processes. Access must be unique, attributable, role-based, least-privilege, purpose-limited, segregated where required, reviewed when role or relationship changes, and automatically or promptly revoked when no longer needed.
Applies to joiner-mover-leaver processes, role changes, representative access, public resource systems, automated provisioning and zero-trust access decisions.

7. Authentication, credentials and sessions
Authentication, MFA, credentials, recovery and sessions

NDIA systems must use unique identifiers, strong and accessible authentication, MFA for privileged, remote, third-party and high-risk access, and risk-based assurance for sessions and transactions. Credentials, passkeys, authentication factors, recovery processes and sessions must be enrolled, protected, rotated, revoked, time-limited and monitored to prevent misuse.
Applies to staff, contractor, provider, partner, participant, remote and high-risk authentication, including passkeys, recovery and transaction-level controls.

8. Privileged access management
Privileged access management and administration

Privileged and administrative access must use approved PAM controls, separate named administrative accounts, MFA, least privilege, just-in-time or time-bound elevation where feasible, approved administrative tools and environments, session logging, monitoring, periodic review and supplier administrator controls.
Applies to administrators, privileged users, identity platform support personnel, supplier administrators and privileged access workstations.
